newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Communist head of Russian Duma cool on Iran ruling.
newsitem.headline: Communist head of Russian Duma cool on Iran ruling.

text.p: The communist head of Russia's State Duma lower house of parliament on Friday issued veiled criticism of a German court verdict accusing Iran of ordering political murders.

"One can take a person to court for a crime he has committed but there is no court in the world which has the authority to carry out a sentence on a whole nation," Gennady Seleznyov told a news conference.
Germany expelled four Iranian diplomats on Thursday after a Berlin court announced its conclusion that Iran had ordered the 1992 murders of Kurdish activists in Berlin.
The European Union, which Moscow said last month it wanted to join, suggested after the verdict that member countries recall their ambassadors from Iran "for consultations".

Seleznyov, who was speaking at a joint news conference with the head of the Iranian parliament, Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri, said the court decision and the Western rebuff had not affected the Iranian's talks in Moscow.

Parliament has no role in shaping foreign policy. But Seleznyov said the conservative legislature did not differ with President Boris Yeltsin and his government on foreign policy, although they disagree on many other issues.
"We are now re-establishing comprehensive ties with...our old allies," he said.

Some Russian officials have said that restoring ties with Moscow's former allies in the third world, weakened after the collapse of the Soviet Union, would help counterbalance NATO's plans to expand eastwards.
Yeltsin met Nateq-Nouri earlier on Friday. The Iranian parliamentary leader is scheduled to meet Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on the last day of his visit on Monday.
